textbookText: Chapter 4 Dynamics The foundations of dynamics were laid at the end of the 16th century by Galileo, who, by experimenting with a smooth ball rolling down an inclined plane, derived the law of motion for falling bodies; he was also the first to recognize that force is the cause of changes in the velocity of a body. Isaac Newton was the first to formulate the fundamental physical laws that govern dynamics in classical non-relativistic physics, especially his second law of motion. Isaac Newton is responsible for the precise formulation of the laws of motion, describing how speed and position vary over a short period of time.

Galileo (Feb 15, 1564 – Jan 8, 1642) 4.1 Introduction Dynamics is a branch of mechanics that deals with the study of the motion of an object by taking its cause. 4.1.1 Force: Activity 4.1 Do the following activities and answer the questions that follow: i) As soon as your class ends, arrange the teaching materials such as the duster and markers on the table and leave the class. ii) Notice the states of those materials on the following day after you enter the class. iii) If you find the states of the body intact, can you guess what’s going on? iv) If you see the states of the body disturbed, write your guess on what the disturbing agents might be.
Physics, Grade 11 | 73

Certainly, when one finds something disturbed in the state, one concludes that an external agent must have either pushed or pulled the objects and disturbed them. This external agent is called the force. Hence, the force is an external agency that causes a change in the state of a body. 4.1.2 Inertia Every object has a tendency to continue in the state it is in, i.e. objects resist the change in their state. This resistance of a body to change its state is called inertia. Inertia is directly proportional to its mass. Therefore, the greater the mass, the greater the inertia, which is expressed by the equation I m where I represents inertia and m represents mass. Examples: i) Suppose there are two water buckets on the ground, one filled with water and the other empty. If a strong wind blows, the empty bucket gets disturbed, while the water-filled bucket remains in the same state. This is due to the greater inertia of the water-filled bucket because of greater mass. It exhibits greater resistance and remains at rest. ii) If a solid iron ball and a hollow rubber ball, both of the same size, are rolling towards you, you will find it easier to stop the hollow one. This is due to its lower mass and less inertia.

Inertia has the following types: Inertia of rest: When the bus driver suddenly accelerates the bus, the passengers in the bus lean backward. This is because they possess the inertia of rest. Inertia of motion: When a moving bus suddenly stops, passengers lean forward due to the inertia of motion. Inertia of direction: A moving bus, when suddenly turns left or right, the passengers lean right or left respectively. It’s because of the inertia of direction, i.e. their resistance to change in direction. 1.1.3 Linear Momentum and Impulse:
Linear Momentum: It describes the motion of a body and is quantified by the product of its mass and velocity. The formula for momentum is given by:

Momentum = mass×velocity Or, p = mv Clearly, change in momentum of a body is due to the change in velocity. A change in velocity, in turn, implies acceleration. A body of mass m hence has some force F acted upon it, and hence the change in momentum is the force according to Newton.
Impulse: Do the activities that follow. i) You slapped a baby’s face. ii) You slipped on a road and iii) Two vehicles suddenly collided.
Consider the common factors among these three events. What result would follow after these occurrences?

Certainly, the result of these three events is what we know as impulse. In all of these events, two common factors are involved: a significant force and a short duration. None of these actions—slapping, slipping, or collision—lasts for an extended period. The effect of a significant force applied for a short duration of time on a body is known as impulse.
